text.tspan: Reading traceroute: what the hops are telling you
You see (one box per hop · row 1 tested, rows 2–4 examples)
It means
Fine (tested): hop 2 doesn't send Time Exceeded,
but hop 3 answers, so the path works.
Stars only in the middle are normal.
Traffic stops after hop 2 (or ICMP is filtered
from there on). Try traceroute -T -p <port>,
then check that network's firewall.
fast
slow
fast
fast
Hop 4 is slow to generate ICMP (low priority on
its control plane), not to forward: no problem.
Only latency that lasts to the destination is real.
Different addresses on the same hop across
probes: load balancing (ECMP) over parallel paths.
Traceroute shows only the forward path: the way back can differ (asymmetric routing).
In AWS, VPC routers don't decrement the TTL or appear: you see instances and gateways, not the fabric.
